blocks.title: Tens and ones
blocks.md: Every number up to 100 is made of **tens** and **ones**. In 47 there are 4 tens and 7 ones. The 4 stands for 40. The 7 stands for 7.

blocks.caption: Three tens and six ones make 36.
blocks.alt: Three green rods and six orange squares.

blocks.title: Break a number
blocks.md: 47 = 40 + 7. 83 = 80 + 3. 60 = 60 + 0. Say it aloud: eighty-three is eight tens and three ones.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- 52 and 25 are different numbers.
- In 60 there are 6 tens and 0 ones.
- Do not read 4 tens 7 ones as 47 tens.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: How many tens and ones are in 58?
steps: The first digit is 5. That is 5 tens.
The last digit is 8. That is 8 ones.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Write the number: 7 tens and 2 ones.

blocks.title: Hundreds
blocks.md: Ten tens make one **hundred**. A number with three digits has **hundreds**, **tens** and **ones**. In 346: 3 hundreds, 4 tens, 6 ones. That is 300 + 40 + 6.

blocks.caption: One hundred, four tens and three ones: 143.
blocks.alt: A blue square, four green rods and three orange squares.

blocks.title: Zero holds a place
blocks.md: In 305 there are 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones. The zero shows there are no tens. 1000 is ten hundreds.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- 305 is not 35. The zero keeps the place.
- 403 and 430 are different.
- 1000 has four digits.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Write 2 hundreds, 5 tens and 1 one as a number.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: What does the 7 stand for in 470?
steps: The 7 is in the middle place: the tens.

blocks.title: Compare
blocks.md: To compare two numbers, look at the **hundreds** first. The bigger hundreds digit wins. If they are the same, look at the tens, then the ones. We use **>** (is greater than) and **<** (is less than).

blocks.caption: 140 is between 100 and 200 on a number line.
blocks.alt: A number line from 100 to 200 in tens with a red dot on 140.

blocks.title: Order
blocks.md: **Ascending** order goes from small to big. **Descending** order goes from big to small. 125 < 152 because the tens 2 is less than 5.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- 99 is less than 100.
- A number with more digits is bigger, if it does not start with 0.
- The sign opens to the bigger number.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Put 405, 54 and 450 in order from small to big.
steps: 54 is the smallest. It has only two digits.

reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Number patterns
blocks.md: We can count in steps. In twos: 2, 4, 6, 8. In fives: 5, 10, 15, 20. In tens: 10, 20, 30. In hundreds: 100, 200, 300.

blocks.caption: Counting in fives to 50.
blocks.alt: A number line from 0 to 50 with marks every five.

blocks.title: Find the rule
blocks.md: Look at two numbers next to each other. How much is added? That is the rule. 20, 25, 30: add 5 each time.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Counting back means take away each time.
- Fives end in 0 or 5.
- Check the rule with every pair.
